scenes.headline: Where should Rotterdam invest first?
scenes.caption: Where should Rotterdam invest first?
scenes.narration: If Rotterdam could prioritise one place next, where would investment have the greatest combined need?

scenes.headline: One city, very different priorities
scenes.caption: 11 indicators. One comparable grid.
scenes.narration: The model compares demographic pressure, income, social vulnerability and access to daily services on the same five-hundred-metre grid.

scenes.headline: The highest-priority cells emerge
scenes.caption: High-priority cells emerge
scenes.narration: Under the balanced scenario, several cells rise because multiple pressures overlap rather than because of one single indicator.

scenes.headline: How high does priority get?
scenes.caption: Priority is relative, not absolute
scenes.narration: The score ranks cells against the rest of this study area, and confidence remains separate from priority.

scenes.headline: Healthy ageing changes the map
scenes.caption: Change the question, change the map
scenes.narration: When healthy ageing gets more weight, older residents, primary care and daily necessities reshape the ranking.

scenes.headline: Social vulnerability shifts priorities again
scenes.caption: Social vulnerability shifts it again
scenes.narration: A social-vulnerability lens gives more weight to low income, benefits and single-parent households.

scenes.headline: But some places stay important in every scenario
scenes.caption: Consensus reveals robust priorities
scenes.narration: The strongest candidates are the places that remain important across several different policy choices.
